policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'will deliver thee for a spoil to the nations', and 'spoil' translates baz (לבז), the qere. The ketiv לבג with gimel yields no word the English could render, so the ASV wording distinguishes the qere reading.

The variant is orthographic: ketiv וקריתמה lacks the yod of qere וְקִרְיָתָֽיְמָה, and both spell the same place name, which ASV gives in its conventional English form 'Kiriathaim'. A transliterated proper name does not distinguish plene from defective spelling, and the only note on the verse is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, in every quarter'), which concerns the English of the frontiers clause and cannot decide a reading. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
